notes: Each eval starts in the fixture's destination Factory repository. Source fixture directories are read-only inputs. The evaluator should inspect the proposed and written destination tree, the migration report, and the unchanged sources.

evals.name: simple-skill-and-script
evals.prompt: Run a migrate-to-Factory task from evals/fixtures/simple/destination. Migrate the release-notes skill and its Python helper from evals/fixtures/simple/source into the existing Factory repository. Preserve behavior and provenance, keep the source read-only, show the mapping before any behavior-changing write, and validate the resulting Factory tree with factory-files.
evals.expected_output: A proposed mapping scopes the release-notes skill and helper to the release role, calls out the approval gate and path adaptation, then writes only under the destination after confirmation. The report distinguishes Factory validation from live apply and confirms the source is unchanged.
assertions: Finds the existing factory.yaml and does not attempt onboarding or live Factory registration.
Inventories both the skill and its helper with stable source-relative provenance.
Proposes a role-scoped destination and keeps the helper bundled with the migrated skill.
Requests confirmation before changing MAIN routing or adding the release role.
Writes only under the destination and reports that the source stayed unchanged.
Uses factory-files for authoring and reports validator exit status without overstating exit 2.

evals.name: multi-repo-multi-role
evals.prompt: From evals/fixtures/multi-repo/destination, migrate the reviewer resources in evals/fixtures/multi-repo/sources/review-workflow and the implementation resources in evals/fixtures/multi-repo/sources/implementation-workflow. Preserve their separate role boundaries and the review-to-implementation handoff. Propose the layout first, do not modify either source, and use factory-files to author and validate the destination.
evals.expected_output: The migration inventory covers both source repositories, maps their distinct roles and scoped resources to separate Factory agents, and adapts the handoff into the existing MAIN agent without introducing a second MAIN. Any conflicting completion semantics are surfaced for confirmation.
assertions: Inventories resources from both repositories and records their separate provenance.
Preserves reviewer and implementer as distinct roles with role-scoped guidance.
Keeps the destination foreman as the only MAIN agent unless replacement is approved.
Maps orchestration and handoffs into MAIN routing rather than copying incompatible workflow syntax.
Surfaces conflicting or incomplete completion semantics instead of silently choosing one.
Does not write to either source repository or operate a live Factory.

evals.name: ambiguity-and-unsupported-features
evals.prompt: Assess the workflow in evals/fixtures/ambiguous/source for migration into evals/fixtures/ambiguous/destination. The source mixes a nightly schedule, an MCP tool, a secret, and unclear reviewer/approver ownership. Produce the inventory and proposed layout, migrate only what is safe in v1, and explain what needs a user decision or manual follow-up.
evals.expected_output: The agent proposes preserving reusable instructions but omits schedules, MCP declarations, and secrets setup. It does not read the secret value, invent a trigger or tool replacement, or choose a role boundary. It stops for confirmation before any behavior-changing write and reports validation only if files were authored and the server actually checked them.
assertions: Classifies schedule, MCP declaration, and secrets setup as intentionally omitted v1 scope.
Never reads or copies a secret value and does not author an MCP declaration.
Identifies reviewer-versus-approver ownership as ambiguous and asks a focused question.
Does not invent an event trigger, substitute tool, or role boundary.
Waits for confirmation before adding roles or changing MAIN routing.
Separates manual follow-ups from server validation and live Factory operation.
